title: Choose the visual world — HBD Summer Party
question: Your brief pins maritime, so every card here lives inside it. No image generation exists on this machine, so this round is code-led: cards carry their identity in palette and facts, not comps. The roll assigned Stern Letters. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Stern Letters
options.lineage: gold-leaf transom lettering on a wooden boat's stern
options.thesis: The invitation is the boat's own nameboard — the name gilded over its hailing port, with five stars cut by the same hand.
options.viewport: A sand-cream boatyard ground, not a dark page. Centred on it, one varnished navy plate: HBD SUMMER PARTY gilded across it in a shaded signwriter's roman, and beneath it the hailing port — 어반피크닉 워터파티룸 · 분당서현. Between the two lines, where a signwriter would gild a rosette, sits a birthday cake with five lit candles drawn in the same gold-leaf grammar and ringed by a life-ring outline: the birthday element is carved into the plate, not pasted on it. Five identical gilt stars run in an even row below. 2026.08.28 FRI 17:00 is incised into the varnish as a cut line. At the bottom edge a real waterline moves in pool aqua.
options.risk: Gold on dark varnish is also whisky and barbershop. If the navy takes the whole page instead of staying a plate on a sand ground, it stops reading as a birthday.

raised.raise: Every section is an incision in the nameboard plate itself — no floating cards, no added containers anywhere on the page.
One reserved hot colour: candle-flame orange appears exactly once, at the cake, and nowhere else.
The what-to-bring list becomes five hand-lettered chandlery tags — equal objects packed edge to edge, never a bulleted list.
The waterline is a genuinely moving medium that displaces, not a decorative wave path.

options.label: The Harbour Almanac
options.lineage: printed tide tables and harbour almanacs
options.thesis: The party as the day's entry in a tide table: high water 17:00, company of five, conditions fair.
options.viewport: One tall almanac page for 2026.08.28. A ruled table gives the day its facts in tabular figures, high water at 17:00 set as the only bold row. Five identical marks run down the margin where an almanac would print its phase symbols. A gilt cake device sits at the head of the sheet as the almanac's own plate engraving.
options.risk: This is also where a careful designer lands. Letterpress calm is the most tasteful answer available, and tasteful calm can under-deliver on warm and playful.

options.label: Street Wood Type
options.lineage: public theater street posters, wood-type capitals at architectural scale
options.thesis: The invitation shouted from a wall: five words in condensed wood-type caps, baselines on diagonals, cropped by the frame.
options.viewport: Five cropped words fill the phone top to bottom — HBD / SUMMER / PARTY / 8.28 / 17:00 — each on its own diagonal, the last one sliced by the edge so your eye finishes it.
options.case: Holds audience identification: everyone reads a shouted poster in one beat, and five words on five diagonals is the Rule of Five for free. Loses product clarity — shouting fights come-as-you-are, the packing list has nowhere quiet to sit, and it abandons the maritime world you pinned.
options.risk: Reads as a rally poster rather than an invitation, and nothing on it is nautical.

options.label: Seven Segment
options.lineage: the seven-segment family: bedside clocks, price totems, scoreboards
options.thesis: The party as a lit time — five cells counting down to 17:00 on a matte panel where unlit segments are designed too.
options.viewport: A rigid cell mask fills the phone. 17:00 sits in fixed slots, five ghost cells lighting one by one as the days close, and the venue rides beneath in a single scoreboard row.
options.case: Holds product clarity on the fact that matters most — a party has exactly one start time, and a countdown states it without a sentence. Loses audience identification for a birthday: a clock panel cannot carry warmth, a packing list, or five people who are all equally the point.
options.risk: Near-black with a red glow is the single most common AI aesthetic, and a clock is not a celebration.

options.label: Curved-Crease Shell
options.lineage: a circular sheet folded along one sweeping crease into a rigid shell
options.thesis: The invitation as one cream disc that rises into a saddle along a single arc.
options.viewport: A cream disc lifting along one charcoal arc, the party facts registered against plan and section views.
options.case: Loses both axes. Close friends heading to a pool party do not identify with deployable geometry, and the facts end up subordinate to a demonstration of curvature.
options.kept: Structural honesty — rigidity earned from the sheet itself, never from added support.

options.label: Raku Smoke-Flash
options.lineage: a red-hot raku vessel lifted into smoke and leaves
options.thesis: The invitation as an unrehearsed carbonized skin, ember orange reserved for what is still hot.
options.viewport: Soot-black ground, crackled white body, one ember-orange region where the page is live.
options.case: Loses both axes. Thermal-shock ceramics has no bearing on a birthday pool party, and an unrehearsed surface fights an invitation's need for exact, trustworthy facts.
options.kept: Reserved hot colour — one temperature, appearing only where the action is.
options.risk: Sombre and funerary for a party.

options.label: VHS Rental Wall
options.lineage: a friday-night video store wall of clamshell spines
options.thesis: The invitation as a genre shelf: five clamshells face-out under fluorescent light.
options.viewport: A packed shelf strip, five boxes face-out, handwritten talkers beneath each.
options.case: Loses both axes. Wrong decade for a 2026 Korean pool party, it overrides the maritime world you pinned, and its central grammar — the gap where a rented box should be — means absence, the exact opposite of five equals all present.
options.kept: Many equal objects packed edge to edge, persuaded by hand-lettered tags.
options.risk: Nostalgia for a decade none of this belongs to.

options.label: Ebru Floated Pigment
options.lineage: pigment combed on a thickened bath, lifted in one contact
options.thesis: The invitation made entirely of moving water, lifted once and never repeated.
options.viewport: A full-frame marbled bath, figures dragged through floating colour, the facts riding the lift.
options.case: Loses on clarity decisively. Water is genuinely on-theme for a pool party, but an irreversible one-pass liquid cannot hold a date, a venue and a packing list in any stable hierarchy, and marbling specifically is not a language this audience reads.
options.kept: Water as a real moving medium rather than a drawn imitation of one.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The modern e-invite, executed impeccably: centred serif name, enormous date, soft summer photograph, one share button.
canonCard.viewport: Name centred at the top, date at display scale beneath it, a soft pool photograph behind a scrim, venue and what-to-bring in a tidy stack, a share button at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other invitation link your friends have opened this year — which is exactly why it is safe.
